findings.title: Client-visibility filtering is bypassed on comments/timeline side-channel endpoints
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636 (read-only). Each nested comments/timeline route now (a) loads the parent with its visibility column and 404s when the parent is not client-visible, then (b) filters module_comments to is_internal=false for client members: approvals.ts:465 and :539 (parent check), :475 (is_internal); assets.ts:361 and :430, :371; findings.ts:464 and :536, :473; proposals.ts:1015 and :1089, :1025. The detail endpoints keep the same predicate (approvals.ts:189, assets.ts:162, findings.ts:164, proposals.ts:145). Regression coverage: apps/api/src/__tests__/client-visibility-sidechannels.test.ts:145-200 (internal parent -> 404 across each path; client-visible parent -> comments query gets .eq('is_internal', false)). Not executed here (node_modules absent); code and tests are present at this commit. Residual (not a re-open): module_timeline_events rows are still returned for a client-visible parent because that table has no per-event internal flag; only status/workflow events are written there.
findings.remediation: No action required for the finding. Optional follow-up: add an is_internal/visibility column to module_timeline_events if any timeline event may ever carry internal-only text.

findings.title: Client-visibility helper fails open and exempts API-key requests
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636. Fail-open half is fixed: apps/api/src/lib/client-visibility.ts:100 throws on the membership query error (previously swallowed) and :107-110 now sets result=true (client-scoped / visibility filter applied) instead of the staff view, logging the regression. The second half is unchanged: :85-92 still returns false (staff view) for any req.apiKey request. The exemption is now documented as a system/integration path (:81-88) and is bounded today because api-keys:manage is an admin-scope permission (supabase/migrations/5302118_permission_matrix_full_catalog.sql:306-307) and the client-role grant loop only grants scope in ('portal','both') (:407-413), so client roles cannot mint keys; the route is also permission-gated (apps/api/src/routes/api-keys.ts:65). It remains a latent bypass if a client-scoped key or a custom role with api-keys:manage is ever introduced.
findings.remediation: Replace the blanket req.apiKey -> staff-view return with the key's own role/tenant scope (e.g. resolve the key creator's membership or store a client/system flag on api_keys), and add a test that a client-capable key cannot see internal rows. Until then, keep api-keys:* out of every client/custom role.

findings.title: NEW: client roles can still read internal comments on tickets and project tasks (is_internal is not enforced on the API or the RLS policy)
findings.evidence: NEW at main@3fa9f636, discovered while re-verifying SEC-P1-011; the defect predates the delta but is in the same class and was not covered by the Nov 3 finding. (1) GET /tickets/:id embeds every comment row with `.select("*, ticket_comments(*)")` without an is_internal predicate (apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:143); GET /tickets/:id/comments returns all rows with only a ticket-org check (tickets.ts:356-378, query at :369-373); neither route carries requirePermission('tickets','view') or an isClientMember filter. (2) GET /projects/:id/tasks/comments applies `.eq('is_internal', false)` only when the caller voluntarily passes ?is_internal=false (apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:845-847); omitting the parameter returns internal notes, and the route has no permission/client gate (:830-851). Client roles hold tickets:view and projects:view (catalog scope 'both', supabase/migrations/5302118_permission_matrix_full_catalog.sql:30,38; client_admin/client_user grant loop at :407-430), and the mct_session cookie is scoped to the parent domain so a client can call the API directly. Intent is unambiguous: the portal UI filters internal rows client-side (apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/support/[ticketId]/page.tsx:172) and the admin ticket form has an 'Internal only' checkbox (apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/page.tsx:562). The DB is not a second line of defence: the ticket_comments SELECT policy is org-membership only (supabase/migrations/5302026_supabase_consolidated_fresh_bootstrap_20260529.corrected.v3.sql:1188-1195). Secondary: POST /tickets/:id/comments accepts isInternal from any caller with tickets:edit (tickets.ts:398-405), so a client_admin can also forge an internal-only note.
findings.remediation: remediated 2026-11-07 via #384

findings.title: NEW: SSO callback forwards the caller's entire cookie jar (including mct_session and csrf_token) to the API when only the PKCE verifier is needed
findings.evidence: NEW at main@3fa9f636 (SSO feature, commits 9d2311e2/306b0ff8). apps/web/app/auth/callback/route.ts:24-27 posts `cookies: request.headers.get("cookie") || ""` to /api/v1/auth/callback. The API uses that blob only to extract the `sb-<ref>-auth-token-code-verifier` cookie (apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:223-229, :249-253); it never needs mct_session, csrf_token or mct_active_org. The session JWT therefore crosses the web->API service boundary inside a JSON body on every login/reset callback. No concrete sink was found at this commit (the API request logger and error handler do not log request bodies, apps/api/src/middleware/request-id.ts, middleware/error.ts:46-52, and Sentry runs beforeSend=scrubSentryEvent with sendDefaultPii=false, apps/api/src/lib/sentry.ts:16-17), so this is least-privilege hygiene, not a proven leak.
findings.remediation: remediated 2026-11-07 via #384

findings.title: NEW: the SSO PKCE start route and the verifier-missing/negative callback paths have no regression tests
findings.evidence: NEW at main@3fa9f636. apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:796-824 (/auth/sso) has no test: grep for 'sso' under apps/api/src/__tests__ and apps/web/__tests__ returns no test for the route or for ssoLoginAction. The added callback suite (apps/api/src/__tests__/auth.test.ts:603-655) covers only the happy path (grant_type=pkce + verifier cookie), a generic 401 on a failed exchange, and the required-auth_code 400; it never asserts that a missing or mismatched code_verifier is rejected, so a future change that drops PKCE binding (e.g. exchanging without the verifier) would not fail CI. No test covers apps/web/lib/auth/auth-actions.ts:45-64 setting the verifier cookie before redirecting.
findings.remediation: remediated 2026-11-07 via #384

findings.title: Restore-test backup location contract (S3_BUCKET/S3_PREFIX) is documented and shared by write/read paths
findings.evidence: The contract is documented at docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:125-146 and in the script headers (scripts/backup-database.sh:5-12, scripts/restore-database.sh:7-11, scripts/backup-storage.sh:6-9). Both restore workflows now call the same discovery helper (db-restore-test.yml:89-111; storage-restore-test.yml:70-89), which normalises a legacy `s3://bucket[/prefix]` value, rebuilds the key once without double-prefixing and emits `backup_file`/`backup_uri` (scripts/ci/find-latest-backup.sh:37-67). The old inline `aws s3 ls | sort | tail -1` duplication is gone. findings.title: Encryption is now enforced, but the offsite/second-destination copy is optional, skipped in the documented dev config, and never verified
findings.evidence: Encryption: both backup workflows set REQUIRE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION=1 (db-backup.yml:109-115; storage-backup.yml:99-103) and both scripts encrypt the gzipped dump/archive with openssl AES-256-CBC/PBKDF2 before upload, deleting the plaintext (scripts/backup-database.sh:108-129; scripts/backup-storage.sh:172-184); both restore paths fail closed on a `.enc` object without the key and decrypt with it (db-restore-test.yml:127-151; scripts/restore-storage.sh:97-109). Offsite: the copy only runs when `S3_OFFSITE_BUCKET` is non-empty (scripts/backup-database.sh:152-159; scripts/backup-storage.sh:206-210), and the scripts now clear that variable whenever bucket+endpoint match the primary (backup-database.sh:49-56; backup-storage.sh:47-54). The documented dev configuration promotes Garage to primary and says the duplicate copy is skipped (docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:135-137), so the current documented state is a single destination; no successful run has produced even the primary object (DR-P0-001). There is also no post-copy `head-object`/listing, so 'Offsite copy complete' only reflects the `aws s3 cp` exit status (backup-database.sh:158; backup-storage.sh:209-210). The docs still tell the operator to 'confirm an encrypted object lands in both buckets' (docs/RTO_RPO.md:50-57), which the promoted-Garage config no longer does by default.
findings.remediation: Decide the intended DR topology: either keep two distinct destinations (different bucket and/or endpoint) and fail the job when the offsite copy is configured but absent, or document that Garage is the single copy and delete the offsite claim. Add a `aws s3api head-object` (size/ETag) check after both uploads and record the destination object keys in the run summary. Do not accept 'copy complete' on the CLI exit code alone.

findings.title: Storage backup listing pagination, partial-download count and archive-integrity gates remain in place

The new ALLOW_EMPTY_STORAGE=1 dev path deliberately reintroduces a manifest-only archive; its monitoring consequence is tracked as DR-P2-010, not as a regression of this row.

Both restore workflows still hard-code `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (db-restore-test.yml:46; storage-restore-test.yml:55) while reading the same repository `S3_ENDPOINT` (db-restore-test.yml:105; storage-restore-test.yml:83), which the secrets matrix documents as the private `http://192.168.222.120:3900` Garage endpoint for dev (docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:135-137) and warns that a GitHub-hosted runner cannot reach (line 188). The matrix scopes BACKUP_RUNNER_LABELS to db-backup/storage-backup only (line 189). findings.title: The dev empty-mirror allowance records a zero-object archive as a successful backup, which the branch-agnostic staleness alarm counts as fresh and the storage restore test is guaranteed to reject
findings.evidence: storage-backup.yml:104-106 sets `ALLOW_EMPTY_STORAGE=1` for every run that is not a prod dispatch or a PROD_BACKUP_ENABLED schedule; scripts/backup-storage.sh:133-139 then writes a manifest-only archive (`object_count: 0`) and the job succeeds, while the restore verifier explicitly refuses any archive with zero object files (scripts/restore-storage.sh:130-133). The independent staleness check does not filter by branch, environment or event — it asks `gh run list --status success --limit 1` across all branches (backup-staleness-check.yml:60-84) — so a dev manifest-only success (or any dev success) satisfies the 30 h 'storage backup' freshness gate for the whole repo, including the prod-backup schedule. The direct prod guard is intact (a prod dispatch or PROD_BACKUP_ENABLED schedule gets `0`), but prod assurance is weakened through the shared success signal. Once a manifest-only archive is the newest object, the next storage-restore-test will select it and fail.
findings.remediation: remediated 2026-11-07 via #383

findings.title: Backup jobs run on persistent lab runners but leave plaintext dumps/downloaded user objects in the workspace when any step fails
findings.evidence: The backup jobs now run on the self-hosted lab runners (db-backup.yml:53; storage-backup.yml:56; run 42345678702 used `ci-runner`). Both scripts clean up only on the success path: scripts/backup-database.sh deletes the plaintext dump only after encryption (:121) and the encrypted object only at the end (:162-163); any pg_dump/verify/encryption/upload/prune failure aborts under `set -e` and leaves `./backups/supabase-dump-*.sql.gz[.enc]` behind. scripts/backup-storage.sh stages downloaded user files under `./storage-backups/<timestamp>/` (:56-69), removes the plaintext tar immediately after encryption (:173-177) but removes the staging directory and encrypted archive only after both uploads (:212); an upload/offsite-copy/prune failure leaves the plaintext staging tree. Neither workflow has an `if: always()` cleanup step (db-backup.yml:55-152; storage-backup.yml:58-133), and neither directory is gitignored, so the files sit in the repo workspace on the runner until the next checkout of this repo cleans them. That is a full plaintext DB dump / user-file set readable by co-tenant processes on a shared lab host after a failure.
findings.remediation: remediated 2026-11-07 via #383

findings.title: Backup retention deletes objects in place with no versioning, object lock or immutability on either destination
findings.evidence: Both scripts prune with `s3api list-objects-v2` + `s3api delete-object` (scripts/backup-database.sh:166-184; scripts/backup-storage.sh:214-231) and retain only 30 days (`RETENTION_DAYS`, backup-database.sh:33; backup-storage.sh:57). No repo-managed bucket has versioning/object-lock for backups: Terraform only versions the Terraform-state bucket (infra/terraform/digitalocean/state-bucket.tf:28-34), and docs/RTO_RPO.md:24-26 documents 30-day retention but no immutability. A bad run, a stolen write key, or a mistaken S3_BUCKET/S3_PREFIX can therefore permanently delete the backup history; there is no tested 'deleted backup' recovery path.
findings.remediation: Enable bucket versioning and a governance/compliance object-lock or lifecycle retention on both backup destinations, and document the recovery procedure (restore a prior object version). Add a drill that deletes a test object and proves it can be recovered, and keep the prune path unable to bypass the lock.

findings.title: The offsite-copy skip ignores S3_OFFSITE_PREFIX, so a same-bucket/different-prefix second copy is dropped; the copy is never verified
findings.evidence: The skip is decided only by bucket+endpoint equality (scripts/backup-database.sh:49-56; scripts/backup-storage.sh:47-54) and then clears `S3_OFFSITE_BUCKET`, even when `S3_OFFSITE_PREFIX` (documented at docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:142-146) differs from `S3_PREFIX`. A legitimate configuration that keeps a second copy under a different prefix in the same bucket is therefore skipped with a 'skipping duplicate copy' message and the offsite prefix is never pruned or written. When the copy does run, the script prints 'Offsite copy complete' immediately after `aws s3 cp` (backup-database.sh:152-158; backup-storage.sh:206-210) with no `head-object`/listing check, so a no-op or wrong-endpoint copy is not detected.
findings.remediation: remediated 2026-11-07 via #389 (offsite prefix comparison + head-object verification)
